html:
The Ka'apor are a Tupi-Guarani people of the Gurupi River region in Maranhão, northeastern Brazil. Their name is often read as "forest dwellers".

They moved into this area in the 1800s from further west in Pará, away from colonists, and fought settlers and gold seekers until the Brazilian Indian Protection Service made peace with them in 1928. They are known for fine featherwork: headdresses, necklaces and ear ornaments in bright colours. Deafness was unusually common among them, and the community developed its own Ka'apor Sign Language, used by deaf and hearing people alike. Today they live on the Alto Turiaçu Indigenous Land, which they patrol against illegal logging. Their Tembé and Guajajara neighbours speak related Tupian languages.
sum: The Ka'apor are a Tupi-Guarani people of the Gurupi River region in Maranhão, northeastern Brazil. Their name is often read as "forest dwellers".
